title: Full blood count
subtitle: Haemoglobin, indices, white cells, differential and platelets
summary: Haemoglobin, indices, white cells, differential and platelets
introduction: Interpret haemoglobin, cell size, white-cell differential and platelets together. Typical ranges below are approximate adult examples and must be replaced by the reporting laboratory’s range.

rows.name: Haemoglobin
lowInterpretation: Anaemia. Assess magnitude, speed of fall, bleeding, haemolysis, renal disease, nutritional deficiency and chronic inflammation.
highInterpretation: Haemoconcentration from reduced plasma volume, smoking or chronic hypoxia; less commonly a primary erythrocytosis.

rows.name: MCV
lowInterpretation: Microcytosis: iron deficiency, thalassaemia or some chronic inflammatory states.
highInterpretation: Macrocytosis: vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis or medication effects.

rows.name: MCH / MCHC
lowInterpretation: Supports hypochromia, commonly seen with iron deficiency.
highInterpretation: MCH may rise with macrocytosis. A markedly raised MCHC can reflect spherocytosis, cold agglutinins or analytical interference.

rows.name: RDW
highInterpretation: Greater variation in red-cell size; may support evolving iron, B12 or folate deficiency, mixed deficiencies or recent transfusion.

rows.name: Total WCC
lowInterpretation: Viral illness, medication or chemotherapy effect, marrow suppression, autoimmune disease or severe sepsis.
highInterpretation: Infection, inflammation, corticosteroids, physiological stress, smoking or haematological disease.

rows.name: Neutrophils
lowInterpretation: Infection risk rises as the count falls. In a patient receiving anticancer treatment, neutrophils ≤0.5 ×10⁹/L with temperature >38°C or features of sepsis is neutropenic sepsis.
highInterpretation: Common with bacterial infection, inflammation, corticosteroids, tissue injury or physiological stress.

rows.name: Lymphocytes
lowInterpretation: Acute illness, corticosteroids, immunodeficiency or treatment effect.
highInterpretation: Often viral infection; persistent or marked elevation may require assessment for lymphoproliferative disease.

rows.name: Eosinophils
highInterpretation: Allergy, asthma, parasitic infection, drug reaction, eosinophilic disease or adrenal insufficiency.

rows.name: Platelet count
lowInterpretation: Bleeding risk depends on count, trajectory and platelet function. Consider sepsis, medication, liver disease, immune destruction, DIC or marrow failure.
highInterpretation: Reactive inflammation, infection, iron deficiency, recent surgery or splenectomy; persistent unexplained elevation may reflect a myeloproliferative disorder.

urgentFindings: Active bleeding, haemodynamic compromise, chest pain, syncope or breathlessness with anaemia.
Rapid haemoglobin fall compared with recent results, even when the current value remains within the laboratory range.
Neutrophils ≤0.5 ×10⁹/L with temperature >38°C or features of sepsis (for example hypotension, new confusion, rigors, reduced urine output or mottled skin) during anticancer treatment.
Platelets very low or falling with spontaneous bleeding, petechiae, melaena, haematuria, neurological symptoms or suspected DIC.
Pancytopenia: low haemoglobin, white cells and platelets together, particularly when new.
overrides: Use the reporting laboratory’s reference ranges and compare with previous results, symptoms, observations, medication and fluid status.

commonPatterns.title: Iron-deficiency anaemia picture
interpretation: Suggests iron deficiency; consider chronic blood loss (GI, menstrual), poor dietary intake or malabsorption
Thalassaemia trait is a differential for microcytosis, particularly when RDW is not raised and the picture is longstanding or in a relevant ethnic background
actions: Ask specifically about GI bleeding (melaena, weight loss, change in bowel habit) and menstrual/obstetric history
Request ferritin and haematinics to confirm iron deficiency (see further testing)
Arrange medical review for further investigation of the bleeding source, particularly in patients over 50 or with new symptoms

commonPatterns.title: Macrocytic anaemia picture
interpretation: Consider vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol excess, liver disease, hypothyroidism or a reticulocyte response to haemolysis/bleeding
Neurological symptoms (paraesthesia, ataxia, cognitive change) can occur with B12 deficiency and may precede the anaemia
actions: Ask about diet, alcohol use, medication and neurological symptoms
Request B12, folate and thyroid function alongside a blood film (see further testing)
Arrange medical review if neurological symptoms are present or the anaemia is marked or symptomatic

commonPatterns.title: Anaemia of chronic disease / inflammation picture
findings: Known chronic inflammatory, infective, renal or malignant condition
interpretation: A normocytic or mildly microcytic anaemia in the context of chronic disease is often multifactorial rather than a single deficiency
Can co-exist with true iron deficiency, which ferritin alone may not reliably distinguish during active inflammation
actions: Correlate with the underlying chronic condition and its current activity/control
Request CRP and haematinics if the cause is unclear (see further testing)
Arrange routine or same-day review depending on symptom burden and trajectory

commonPatterns.title: Reactive neutrophilia / infection picture
findings: Clinical signs or symptoms of infection or inflammation
interpretation: Common and usually reflects bacterial infection, inflammation, tissue injury or a physiological/steroid-driven response rather than primary haematological disease
actions: Correlate with clinical source, observations and CRP (see further testing)
Treat the underlying cause per local sepsis/infection pathway if clinically indicated
Reassess if the count remains markedly raised or rises further despite treatment

commonPatterns.title: Unexplained thrombocytopenia picture
findings: Platelet count below the normal range
No clear precipitant such as recent chemotherapy, known liver disease or sepsis
interpretation: Consider immune thrombocytopenia, medication effect, liver disease, hypersplenism, marrow infiltration or, if other cell lines are also affected, marrow failure
Bleeding risk depends on the count, trajectory and platelet function, not the count alone
actions: Review medication list for known causes of drug-induced thrombocytopenia
Examine for bleeding, bruising, petechiae, splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy
Arrange medical review for further work-up; treat as urgent if bleeding, a very low count, or other cell lines are also abnormal (see urgent findings)

commonPatterns.title: Possible lymphoproliferative picture
findings: Abnormal differential or atypical cells flagged by the laboratory
Systemic features such as lymphadenopathy, weight loss, night sweats or fatigue
interpretation: Most lymphocytosis is reactive (viral illness), but persistence, a very high count, or systemic ('B') symptoms raise the possibility of a lymphoproliferative disorder
This distinction usually cannot be made on the FBC alone
actions: Examine for lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly and systemic symptoms
Arrange medical review for further investigation, including a blood film (see further testing)
Safety-net and arrange follow-up FBC if the picture is otherwise well and improving

rationale: Reviews red-cell morphology, white-cell differential and platelet appearance directly, which can identify a cause (e.g. iron deficiency, haemolysis, blasts, atypical lymphocytes) that the automated count alone cannot
Confirms and distinguishes iron, B12 and folate deficiency as causes of microcytic or macrocytic anaemia
Distinguishes a marrow response (e.g. haemolysis, acute bleeding) from marrow failure or a hypoproliferative anaemia
Supports assessment of an infective or inflammatory driver of a raised white-cell count or anaemia of chronic disease
Identifies renal or hepatic disease that can contribute to anaemia, and provides baseline organ function before further investigation or treatment
A single result can be misleading — trend over serial results helps confirm whether an abnormality is improving, stable, evolving or an artefact before further escalation

specimens.notes: Whole blood — purple/lilac-top EDTA tube, 3 mL. Do not use a heparinised tube — heparin can cause platelet clumping and affect the film.
